FEATURE / VOXEL IMPORT PIPELINE ISSUE: Add a reusable authoring pipeline that can take a conventional detailed Unity-compatible triangle mesh and convert it into the repository's canonical destructible voxel representation while preserving the source model's recognizable shape, curved silhouette, proportions, major surface detail, and material/color regions as closely as the voxel resolution permits. Prove the pipeline on a downloaded detailed dragon model and present the original mesh and voxelized result together in the built `VoxelShowcase` for direct visual comparison. This is not complete merely because a dragon-shaped voxel volume exists; the voxelized dragon must closely resemble the specific downloaded source model under human visual review.

SOURCE DRAGON / LICENSING: Download a detailed, non-voxel-native dragon model from a reputable asset source. The source must be a conventional curved polygonal mesh with enough detail to make the conversion meaningful: a clearly modeled head/snout, neck, torso, limbs, feet/claws, wings, tail, and multiple secondary silhouette features such as horns, spines, fins, scales/plates, or similarly readable anatomy. Prefer a source of roughly 20k+ triangles when practical; do not choose a deliberately blocky, Minecraft-like, primitive, or extremely low-poly dragon simply to make the comparison easy. A current candidate is the Sketchfab model `Black Ink Dragon - Stylized Model` by Meleagor (approximately 21.6k triangles, CC Attribution at the time this issue was authored): https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/black-ink-dragon-stylized-model-041c76b2bb4f4a5ca5fe035e05e30c95 . The implementer may use a different model if it is at least comparably detailed and better suited to the pipeline.

Before downloading/committing any third-party asset, verify the license at implementation time. Prefer CC0 or CC-BY. Do not use a non-commercial asset, a franchise rip, an asset whose terms prohibit repository redistribution, or an asset with ambiguous rights. Record the exact source URL, author, license, downloaded source format, source triangle/vertex count, and a checksum of the downloaded file in durable repository attribution/documentation. Preserve all attribution/license files required by the source. If the source license does not permit committing the original asset, select a different source rather than depending on an untracked local file.

ARCHITECTURE / SOURCE-OF-TRUTH CONSTRAINT: The final dragon must become normal repository voxel data. The imported polygon mesh is authoring input/reference only and must never become a second runtime geometry truth for destruction, collision, networking, or gameplay. The repository architecture requires deterministic CPU-side integer authoritative state and discrete voxel occupancy/material state; rendering is presentation and collision derives from the same voxel cells. The conversion tool may inspect Unity mesh positions, normals, UVs, submeshes, textures, and transforms during offline/editor authoring, but it must bake a canonical voxel asset/stamp/volume before runtime. Runtime/server behavior must not depend on GPU rasterization, the source triangle mesh, floating-point SDF state, a hidden MeshCollider, or a second non-voxel copy of the dragon.

REUSABLE MESH-TO-VOXEL IMPORTER: Implement this as a reusable editor/build authoring capability in the shared voxel/world-authoring layer, with a clear API that accepts a Unity `Mesh`, imported model hierarchy, or equivalent source object plus configuration such as target voxel size/resolution, transform/scale, material mapping, occupancy policy, and thin-feature preservation policy. Do not write a dragon-specific voxel generator and do not manually place thousands of dragon voxels. The same pipeline must be capable of voxelizing another arbitrary static prop or creature mesh. If a source is skinned/rigged, it is acceptable for this first feature to bake a chosen static pose to a mesh before voxelization, but that step must be explicit and reusable rather than dragon-specific.

GEOMETRY CONVERSION REQUIREMENTS: Convert source triangles into discrete occupied voxel cells with a robust conservative surface rasterization and an interior-fill strategy appropriate for closed or nearly closed meshes. Correctly honor nested transforms, non-uniform source hierarchy transforms where supportable, mirrored axes/orientation, model pivot, and source bounds. Avoid holes, disconnected islands, missing body sections, or accidental filled voids caused by naive vertex-only sampling. The algorithm must inspect triangle coverage, not merely quantize source vertices. Preflight the source for non-manifold/open geometry and either handle it predictably or report a clear authoring error/fallback; silent corruption is not acceptable.

CURVES / RESOLUTION / THIN FEATURES: The purpose of this issue is specifically to show that conventional curved forms survive voxelization convincingly. Choose a dragon world scale and voxel resolution high enough that the head profile, curved neck/back, wing leading/trailing edges, tail arc/taper, limbs, horns/spines, and claws remain recognizable from normal showcase viewing distances. Use supersampling/conservative triangle coverage or another justified authoring technique where useful, but the baked result must still resolve to the normal discrete voxel state. Thin-feature handling may conservatively retain a source feature that intersects a voxel even when its center does not, but it must not globally inflate the model until wings, horns, legs, or tail become visibly too thick. If the current global voxel scale cannot preserve the required silhouette at the dragon's chosen physical size, scale the showcase dragon to a substantial creature size or improve the importer; do not change authoritative world voxel semantics solely for this example.

INTERIOR / SOLIDNESS: The resulting dragon must behave as a solid voxel object where the source represents a solid body. A cut/destruction through the torso should expose voxel interior rather than reveal that only a one-cell surface shell was imported, unless the shared engine has an explicit supported hollow-volume semantic and the source is intentionally hollow. Wing membranes and other genuinely thin surfaces may use a documented minimum-thickness/conservative policy so they survive discretization.

MATERIAL AND COLOR PRESERVATION: Preserve the source model's major visual material/color regions where the source provides usable materials or textures. The importer should sample source submesh/material identity and, where practical, base-color texture/UV information into the voxel material palette or a generated/import mapping. The exact source texture does not need to survive texel-for-texel, but the voxelized dragon should not collapse a multicolored/material-separated source into a single arbitrary solid color if doing so materially reduces resemblance. Material mapping must be deterministic once baked and must use the normal voxel material system. Record any palette quantization decisions.

BAKED OUTPUT / REUSE: Store the result in the existing sparse voxel/brick representation or a reusable serialized voxel stamp/asset that populates that representation through normal WorldBuilder/shared systems. Do not serialize a dense full-volume array if the existing sparse representation can avoid it. The baked dragon should be placeable multiple times at arbitrary transforms supported by the world-authoring system without re-running expensive triangle voxelization at runtime. The source mesh may remain in the project only as licensed authoring/reference content and for the explicit showcase comparison; gameplay placement must use the voxelized artifact.

VOXELSHOWCASE COMPARISON DISPLAY: Add a clearly labeled `Mesh -> Voxels` comparison area to the built `VoxelShowcase`. Present the downloaded original dragon mesh and the voxelized dragon side-by-side in the same static pose, same effective world scale, same orientation, same ground/contact plane, and comparable neutral lighting. Give both enough spacing that silhouettes do not overlap. The camera must be able to inspect the pair closely without clipping. A viewer should immediately understand which is `Source Mesh` and which is `Voxelized`, using in-world labels/UI that do not obscure the models. Do not rely on the mountain dragon placeholder from another SceneIssue as the only comparison location. This issue owns a dedicated comparison presentation so its visual acceptance can be evaluated independently.

VISUAL VALIDATION IS A HARD GATE: Human review of the rendered built application is mandatory. Before this issue can move to pending, capture durable source-vs-voxel comparison images from at least: (a) front, (b) left or right side, (c) rear, (d) front three-quarter, (e) rear three-quarter, and (f) an elevated/top three-quarter view. Use matched camera FOV, distance, pose, scale, ground plane, and lighting for the two models in each comparison. Also capture close-up comparisons of the head/horns, one wing including its edge/membrane shape, feet/claws, and tail taper. Save the captures with the SceneIssue evidence so a reviewer does not have to trust prose or test logs.

The reviewer must explicitly inspect: overall body proportions; head and snout profile; horn/spine placement; neck/back curvature; wing count, span, sweep, leading/trailing edge shape, and membrane thickness; limb count, placement, joint bends, feet and claws; tail length, curvature, and taper; chest/belly/body mass; major negative spaces between limbs/wings/body; grounding/contact; and major material/color regions. The voxel dragon must be unmistakably the same specific dragon model, not merely another generic dragon. Curved areas may show expected voxel stair-stepping at close range, but there must be no gross silhouette changes, missing anatomy, fused limbs, severed wing sections, large holes, obvious interior leaks, floating voxel islands, materially bloated thin features, or incorrect orientation.

QUANTITATIVE SIMILARITY SUPPORT: Add automated geometric comparison as supplemental evidence, not a replacement for visual review. At minimum, sample the source surface and the baked voxel surface in normalized model space and report a symmetric surface-distance metric. Target a 95th-percentile source-to-voxel surface distance of no more than approximately 1.5 target voxels and investigate any maximum-error clusters that correspond to visible anatomy. Also render or compute binary silhouettes from the same fixed front/side/three-quarter validation cameras and require a strong overlap threshold, targeting IoU >= 0.90 for the primary views unless a documented thin-feature limitation makes one view slightly lower. Do not lower thresholds simply to pass; if a metric disagrees with obvious visual defects, the visual defect still fails acceptance. Record metric values with the issue evidence.

BEHAVIORAL REGRESSION COVERAGE: Add focused tests through the production importer/WorldBuilder path. Include synthetic geometry that proves triangle coverage and interior fill (for example sphere/cylinder/closed curved shapes rather than only boxes), repeat-conversion stability for the same input/configuration, transform/orientation handling, material mapping, and thin-feature retention. Add a dragon-specific regression against the checked-in source/baked artifact that proves required anatomical regions are non-empty and spatially plausible without reducing the test to raw voxel counts or source-string checks. Where practical, verify that the same baked artifact can be placed through normal WorldBuilder composition and participates in the same occupancy/collision queries as authored world voxels.

DESTRUCTION / WORLD-TRUTH CHECK: In a built-app validation copy/instance of the voxelized dragon, perform at least one normal voxel edit/destruction action against the body and demonstrate that the edit affects the same canonical voxel cells used for rendering/collision. The source mesh must not remain behind as an indestructible visual shell, and collision must not continue to follow the original triangle mesh after voxel cells are removed. This can be a supplemental validation instance separate from the pristine comparison pair.

PERFORMANCE / BLAST RADIUS: Measure and record source import/voxelization time, baked occupied-voxel count, sparse brick/chunk count, serialized asset size, resident memory when placed, and incremental render/world-build cost for the dragon comparison. Check triangle/raymarch/render cost, streaming implications, collision query behavior, and supported device budgets. Expensive mesh-to-voxel work should occur offline/editor-side, not during ordinary runtime world generation. Do not weaken existing device or world-build budgets to make this feature pass. Ensure importer changes do not alter existing terrain/building voxelization or normal world truth semantics unexpectedly.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) A legitimately licensed, conventional detailed curved dragon mesh is downloaded, committed with required attribution/license metadata, and documented with source URL, author, license, format, triangle/vertex count, and checksum.
(2) The chosen source is meaningfully detailed and non-voxel-native; it includes a readable head, body, wings, limbs/feet, tail, and secondary silhouette detail so curved-shape fidelity is genuinely tested.
(3) A reusable shared mesh-to-voxel authoring/import pipeline converts source triangle geometry into canonical discrete voxel occupancy/material data; no dragon-specific hand-authored voxel sculpture is used.
(4) The importer robustly rasterizes triangle surfaces and fills intended solid interiors, handles source transforms/orientation, and does not rely on vertex quantization alone.
(5) Curved silhouette and thin anatomy survive at an appropriate voxel resolution: head profile, neck/back curves, wing edges, limbs, horns/spines, claws, and tail are recognizable and proportionally faithful.
(6) Major source material/color regions are preserved or intentionally palette-quantized through the normal voxel material system.
(7) The baked dragon is stored/instantiated through the normal sparse voxel/WorldBuilder systems and can be reused without runtime triangle voxelization.
(8) Built `VoxelShowcase` presents source mesh and voxelized result side-by-side at matched pose, scale, orientation, ground contact, and lighting with clear labels.
(9) Durable built-app comparison captures exist for front, side, rear, front three-quarter, rear three-quarter, elevated/top three-quarter, plus close-ups of head/horns, wing, feet/claws, and tail. Human review confirms the voxel result closely resembles the exact source model and contains no major missing/fused/bloated/broken anatomy or gross silhouette errors.
(10) Supplemental geometric similarity evidence reports symmetric source-vs-voxel surface distance with 95th-percentile error targeted <= 1.5 voxels and primary-view silhouette IoU targeted >= 0.90; visible defects cannot be waived merely because aggregate metrics pass.
(11) Focused behavioral regressions exercise the production importer using curved synthetic geometry plus the dragon artifact, covering surface rasterization, interior fill, repeat-conversion stability, transforms, material mapping, thin-feature retention, and normal WorldBuilder placement. Source-string/count-only assertions are insufficient as sole proof.
(12) A built-app destruction/world-truth check proves the voxelized dragon edits/destructs as canonical voxels and that neither rendering nor collision secretly continues to use the original polygon mesh.
(13) The exact built-application `VoxelShowcase` harness reaches a usable rendered scene without startup/runtime exceptions and records the comparison evidence from the actual built player, not only the Unity editor.
(14) Import time, occupied voxel count, sparse brick/chunk count, baked size, runtime memory, and render/world-build cost are recorded and remain within repository budgets; ordinary runtime does not perform expensive source-mesh voxelization.
(15) Final closure requires direct human visual inspection of all required captures. If the voxel result is only generically dragon-like, loses major curved forms, or does not closely resemble the downloaded source, the issue remains open and the importer/resolution must be improved.

RELATION TO EXISTING MOUNTAIN DRAGON FEATURE: `20260828-180417-000-VoxelShowcaseMountainDragonCutscene` currently allows a placeholder dragon and is a separate assignment. Do not modify that SceneIssue's metadata or scope from this task. This feature should produce a reusable voxel dragon asset suitable for later replacing such placeholders, but this issue's completion is proven in its own comparison area and must not depend on another agent's ticket.
